shadow_trades.reasoning_summary: I currently have equal amounts (1 each) of C, A, and B. Trading away my only A for another B would leave me with 0 A and 2 B, reducing variety and utility. Since I value variety, this trade would not improve my bundle.

I currently have equal amounts (1 each) of C, A, and B. Trading away my only B for an extra A would leave me with 0 B and 2 A, reducing variety and utility since I already have 1 A. This trade doesn't improve my bundle.

Current inventory is 1/1/1, perfectly balanced. Trading away my only B for 2 more A would leave me with 0 B and 3 A, creating a lopsided bundle (0,3,1) which reduces variety value even though total items increase. I'd rather keep balance or trade for something that maintains diversity.

Trading away my only A for another B would leave me with 0 A and 2 B, reducing variety (1,1,1 to 0,1,2), which lowers utility given my preference for balanced holdings.

I currently have equal quantities of C, A, and B (1 each). Trading away my only C for another B would leave me with 0 C and 2 B, reducing variety and utility. Since I value variety, this trade would not improve my bundle.

Currently I have C:2, A:1, B:0. Trading away my only A for B would leave me with C:2, A:0, B:1 — still uneven and I'd lose my only unit of A while just gaining a unit of B, not improving variety balance. Better to seek a trade that adds B without depleting A entirely, e.g., trading C for B instead.
I currently have 2 C, 1 A, 0 B. Trading 1 C for 1 B moves me to 1 C, 1 A, 1 B, a perfectly even distribution, which maximizes value given my preference for variety.

Giving up 2 C for 1 B would leave me with 0 C, 1 A, 1 B - trading away all of one good is too extreme. I'd rather do a 1-for-1 trade to balance my inventory (C:2, A:1, B:0) toward variety without depleting C entirely.

Since I value variety, I'd rather keep A and acquire B without giving up my only unit of A, or find a trade that improves balance rather than just shifting the imbalance to a different good.

I currently have C:2, A:1, B:0. Trading away 1 C (of which I have surplus) for 1 B (which I have none of) improves variety and balances my bundle to C:1, A:1, B:1 - a more even and thus more valuable distribution under my preference for variety.

Giving up all my C (2) for just 1 B would leave me with 0 C, 1 A, 1 B - trading a scarcity advantage for another scarcity, but at a 2:1 ratio that's too costly. I'd rather propose a 1:1 trade of C for B to balance my inventory without overpaying.
